Q: rust Command fails in build.rs (No such file or directory) A:

Turns out I must pass the arguments in the args() or arg() function. So instead of.

Command::new("bun run build")
//  .etc()

It should be.

Command::new("bun")
    .args(["run", "build"])

Q: How do I add weekdays to a date in Joda-Time A:

tl;dr

myLocalDate.with( org.threeten.extra.Temporals.nextWorkingDay() )

Joda-Time supplanted by java.time

The Joda-Time project is now in maintenance-mode, its creator Stephen Colebourne having gone on to lead the JSR 310 project that added java.time classes to Java 8+.

ThreeTen-Extra

Stephen Colebourne also leads the ThreeTen-Extra project, a library that extends the java.time with additional functionality.

org.threeten.extra.Temporals.nextWorkingDay()

In that library, you will find the TemporalAdjuster implementation, nextWorkingDay. That adjuster returns the next working day, ignoring Saturday and Sunday.

final java.time.temporal.TemporalAdjuster nextWorkingDayAdjuster = org.threeten.extra.Temporals.nextWorkingDay() ;
LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse( "2025-01-03" ) ;      // Friday.
LocalDate next = date.with( nextWorkingDayAdjuster ) ;  // Monday, January 6, 2025.

Q: Lookup multiples values from another table A:

You need to join Table1 and Table2 and alias your columns to the naming you desire:

select Table1.ID, Table1.rule_id_1, Table2_1.rule_name as rule_id_1_Name, Table1.rule_id_2, Table2_2.rule_name as rule_id_2_Name
from Table1
join Table2 Table2_1
on Table1.rule_id_1 = Table2_1.rule_id
join Table2 Table2_2
on Table1.rule_id_2 = Table2_2.rule_id

Explanation:

  • we load from Table1
  • join with Table2, representing the first rule, aliased as Table2_1
  • on the condition that rule_id_1 of Table1 matches rule_id of Table2_1
  • join with Table2, representing the second rule, aliased as Table2_2
  • on the condition that rule_id_2 of Table1 matches rule_id of Table2_2

Please note that if a record in Table has no match either for the first or the second rule in Table2, then it won't appear among the results. If you want to have semi-orphans or orphans like this as well in the results, use left join instead of join.

Q: save excel worksheet with empty strings instead of Nonetype with python A:

I just had the same issue and solved it using the win32com library, which enables you to set the cell value directly without any further conversion happening in the background:

import win32com.client
import pythoncom

...

# Initialize COM
pythoncom.CoInitialize()

try:
    # Get absolute path
    excel_path = os.path.abspath(excel_path)
    
    # Start Excel application
    excel = win32com.client.Dispatch("Excel.Application")
    excel.Visible = False  # Run in background
    excel.DisplayAlerts = False  # Suppress alerts
    excel.ScreenUpdating = False
    
    # Open workbook
    wb = excel.Workbooks.Open(excel_path)
    
    # enforce text format and write empty strings instead of None
    for ws in wb.Worksheets:
        used_range = ws.UsedRange
        if used_range.Count > 0:
            for row in used_range.Rows:
                for cell in row.Cells:
                    # set text format
                    cell.NumberFormat = "@"
                    # write actual empty string directly to cell
                    if cell.Value is None:
                        cell.Value2=""

    # Save and close
    wb.Save()
    wb.Close()
    excel.Quit()
    
finally:
    # Cleanup COM
    pythoncom.CoUninitialize()

The trick is to access the cell value via "cell.Value2" instead of "cell.Value" when writing. This way is more direct, i.e. no "smart" conversion happens in the background converting empty strings to None, as it is the case when setting the value via "cell.Value" or when using openpyxl to write.

Q: Enabling Next.js HMR on Windows Without Polling or WSL Filesystem A:

True HMR on Windows depends entirely on native filesystem events. When your source code is watched by tools running inside WSL or a Linux container, those tools cannot receive real file change notifications from the Windows NTFS filesystem, so they inevitably fall back to polling. This is a hard technical limitation of the WSL2 and Docker filesystem bridges, not a misconfiguration in Next.js.

To get instant, event-based HMR, the project files must live on Windows NTFS, and Next.js must run using Windows Node or Bun, started from PowerShell or CMD. In this setup, Next.js can use Windows’ native file-watch APIs, which enables true HMR without polling. PostgreSQL can remain in Docker with ports exposed to localhost, because the database layer does not affect file watching.

Nginx should be treated only as a reverse proxy and must not participate in file watching or dev restarts. Any environment variables or webpack options that force polling should be removed. In short, if any part of the dev server that watches files runs across a virtualization boundary, true HMR is impossible; running the app natively on Windows with files on NTFS is the only reliable solution.
